title: 2X

source.rights_note: Publicly accessible screenplay; retain analysis and metadata only until reuse rights are confirmed.

story.logline: A financial trader moving through a rushed city suddenly experiences the world at double speed, turning an ordinary commute into a crisis of control and perception.
story.theme: systemic acceleration, loss of control and attention
story.character_goal: The Trader wants to reach work prepared for an important morning meeting.
story.obstacle: The city and its people accelerate around him while he remains at normal speed.
story.turning_choice: He stops treating the anomaly as background noise, changes the podcast speed and begins investigating what is happening.
story.result: The commute becomes a visual and conceptual crisis; the available excerpt establishes the problem and investigation rather than a final resolution.

beats.visible_action: The Trader moves through a crowded commute while listening to a market crash podcast.
beats.state_out: economic and temporal anxiety is planted
beats.evidence: podcast warnings and repeated crowd friction

beats.visible_action: The crowd begins moving twice as fast while the Trader struggles to keep pace.
beats.state_out: the world follows a new speed rule
beats.evidence: repeated 2x action and altered crowd movement

beats.visible_action: The Trader tests the podcast speed and confirms that the environment remains accelerated.
beats.evidence: he changes playback speed and compares the result

beats.visible_action: He pauses at crossings and observes people, trains and a homeless man moving unnaturally fast.
beats.evidence: the character begins testing the system rather than merely reacting

scene_functions: make the rule progressively harder to ignore
rules_observed: A repeated formal device can become story information when its effect on the protagonist changes.
anti_patterns: Speed effects without a character objective would become a montage rather than a story.
quality_notes: Strong visual premise and continuity rule; useful model for turning a visual effect into a narrative constraint.
